complexity.notes: The bare `except` around the comparison loops is poor style and swallows unrelated errors; the entire comparison could be replaced by `return multiset_s == multiset_t` (or simply `return Counter(s) == Counter(t)`), since dict equality already handles missing keys. An early `len(s) != len(t)` check would also short-circuit obvious non-anagrams.
complexity.summary: Builds per-character frequency dictionaries for both strings, then compares the two multisets key by key, treating a missing key (KeyError) as a mismatch. Since the alphabet is fixed at 26 lowercase letters, the dictionaries hold at most 26 entries, so counting is linear in the string length and extra space is constant.
